answer: Each agent identity should anchor to a refundable stake and a verifiable work history, rather than to a free username. A new identity starts with low limits and gains trust only after completing useful, audited tasks over time. Reaching the zenith of access requires sustained honest behaviour, not merely creating accounts. An attacker who wants many influential identities must fund a separate stake for each, wait through the same slow history, and risk losing every deposit if peers detect fraud. So cost rises with the summit sought, making a Sybil swarm far pricier than one honest agent.
